reviews.review: big pretty open galaxy game some space explore mostly rpg seems to be a good storyline with lots of npc interaction. Similar to other mass effects but i actually like it more. the graphics are very good.

It's not a bad game per se. The first 8-10 hours are great. Before you land on a second planet. It's compact story telling, in class with the other Mass Effect games. 

When you've landed on the second planet, you notice same pattern like many other open world games suffer from. It's big. But it's stretched so damn thin. 
You open your map, see points to talk to. Get shallow missions you really don't care about in any way more than that you want to remove dots from the map. 
You open the map, drive to the nearest dot, pick something up, talk to someone, scan something, or shoot 4-5 guys. Then you open the map, drive to the nearest dot, pick something up, talk to someone, scan something, or shoot 4-5 guys. A hundred mundane missions later you talk to someone you've forget you've talked to and he or she thank you for taking care of it. 
You don't know which mission it was, you don't care what mission it was, and you don't care about the micro story that character is talking about - and as in many of these games, they make no sense. You take down a head quarter of the enemy, but shooting up a small camp is still there as a mission even though story-wise that camp should've been over run. 
It's 80% of the playtime. 
On top off that bugs. You drive your boring as car to some boring as icon, to scan some boring as face, to skip his boring as line so the mission completes, just for the face not being there. 


I'd really like to play a cut version of this game, that only included missions with story. A fifth the length. But those hours fun and intriguing gameplay. Not grindingly driving around scanning downed drowns scattered around the planet for hours just to not miss some actually good mission. 

I really wish this was a good game since I love the original Mass Effect games. But these open world copy paste games really is a curse on the gaming world. It tricks people into thinking they are actually good games because of long play time. Even though those hours sucked.
Good game otherwise ruined by the stupid EA launcher app nightmare.

(Over 600 hours on other platforms)

IT'S NOT THE TRILOGY, IT WASN'T SUPPOSED TO BE.

It's easy to look back on the original Mass Effect game with rose colored glasses, but it had a lot of issues too, ME didn't hit its stride until the sequel. Whatever you take away from other reviews, it's apples and oranges. Andromeda is its own beast. If it had gotten its DLC and sequels, I think people would be singing a different tune about it. It needed that time to mature, but people never gave it a chance.

People complain about shallow characters. Well, you get to know the characters just fine, and in ME1, the non-romances barely had anything to say. For instance, people love Wrex so much but aboard the Normandy, he barely has two words to say the entire game.

The characters in this game are more fleshed out than ME1 characters, and while they are not ready for one of the big conversations with your character Ryder, they can be found moving about the ship having conversations with one another. Party banter in the field is also constant and high quality, though eventually they will run out of things to say, it can take quite a while, and this just encourages you to try different squad combos to see how they interact. Ryder even jumps in on some of those conversations.

Andromeda does have a lighter tone than the original trilogy. The protagonist is younger and less sure of themselves, but you see as you play through the game, the way Ryder interacts with people becomes more confident and commanding. You don't start off with Shepard who is almost 10 years older with as many times experience, Ryder has to come into their own during the course of the story, gaining confidence and a command style. Also remember this is still effectively a civilian operation in Andromeda, your character has experience in the Alliance, but they aren't some war hero.

Andromeda's skill, class, and combat systems are dramatically improved. You can take any talent on any character, so if you are starting off, you can immediately start focusing purely on combat, biotics or tech, or mix them. Then you activate "profiles" like Adept, Vanguard, etc. that give bonuses to those things.

Combat is fast paced, intense, and smooth. Cover is activated by merely being near something (with a satisfying *thunk* to tell you Ryder has leaned against the cover), and the jump jet adds a verticality to combat that didn't exist in the previous games. You can even build for jump jet combat.

The game has an extensive looting and crafting system that lets you further customize how you want to play, including weapon mods that can make them full auto, burst, single fire, or even use classic heat sinks that refill over time like ME1.

The story isn't as cohesive as the trilogy, but again I think if Andromeda had gotten its sequels, we would be looking back differently on it. The story starts off strong, drags a bit in the middle, and finishes strong. The middle is reinforced by some pretty good local planet storylines (Kadara in particular has a strong story) and even moreso by the squadmate personal quests, which are all unique and have a lot of great interactions, a couple of them are quite funny, Liam's in particular.

Also, I don't get bugs, so I don't know what other people are coming from saying the game is buggy.

TLDR: It doesn't quite measure up to the trilogy, but it's pretty hard for a single proof of concept that was rushed out of development to stack up to an epic story that spanned three games. Don't play Andromeda expecting the original trilogy, go into it expecting Andromeda, and you'll do fine Pathfinder.
